newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- ANGLO AMERICAN SET FOR ASSET SALE

Mining group Anglo American is considering the disposal of a number of non-core assets. The proposals are the likely outcome of a strategic review launched by the group in response to the changes in South Africa following the end of apartheid. Anglo, the largest mining group in the world, dominates the South African economy and, through a web of cross-shareholdings, controls companies which total almost 40 percent of the Johannesburg stock market.
-- MIDLAND TO USE ELECTRONIC SCANNER TO CLEAR CHEQUES

Midland Bank has contracted computer services group Unisys to develop a system for electronic scanners to process cheques for clearing. The bank expects the move to cut the costs of processing cheques by 45 percent, to speed up the process, and to cut down on errors. Initially the scanners will deal with cheques which have been printed, but more advanced software is expected which will also be able to read the amounts written in longhand.
-- UK AND NORWAY REOPEN GAS TALKS

Britain's new energy minister, Lord Fraser, has made a priority the breaking of the impasse between Britain and Norway over Norwegian gas exports. The British government is refusing to authorise any new gas imports into the country, a policy which has seen Norway move from supplying about 27 percent of UK gas demand in 1985 to just 2 percent now.
-- BRUSSELS MOVES TO FREE TEXTILES ANGERS INDUSTRY

A proposal by the European Commission to accelerate the liberalisation of Europe's textiles and clothing market - without reciprocal market opening - has angered executives in the industry. They are concerned that if the Commission forces through the measure unilaterally, it will lose out on a lever with which to pry open markets that remain closed to European exports.
-- FOREX DEALS MAKE DEBUT ON INTERNET

Currency Management Corporation, a London-based foreign exchange market-maker, is launching currency speculation on the Internet. It will offer wealthy investors the opportunity to place orders using the Internet. However, the project has yet to receive authorization from the Securities and Futures Authority so its UK customers are not protected by the Investors Currency Scheme.
-- VISA ISSUERS TARGET COMPANIES

The UK's Visa card issuers are hoping to be able to offer their services to corporate buyers. The card issuers have been in talks with Customs and Excise over allowing corporate buyers to switch to plastic for their purchases, rather than sticking with paper purchasing orders and invoices. The paper system is deemed necessary in order to keep records for VAT calculations. A decision from Customs and Excise is expected next week.
-- EUROTUNNEL BANKS TO GAIN 49 PERCENT STAKE

The 225 creditor banks which have loaned the troubled channel tunnel operator Eurotunnel 9 billion stg are to gain just under 49 percent control of the group by converting 2 billion stg of the loans into equity. The deal, part of a refinancing agreement made by the banks and Eurotunnel last week, will be presented to shareholders on Monday.
-- SIEBE TO REVAMP VEHICLE ACTIVITIES

Components company Siebe, which manufactures controls and appliances, is to reveal a major reorganization of its automotive activities. The company is aiming to take advantage of the trend within the automotive industry for carmakers to ask component groups to supply entire subsystems ready for assembly. Siebe is to create a new automotive division employing 6000 people at manufacturing sites in Europe, the Pacific Rim, and North and South America.
-- ITALY DUE TO REVEAL SCALE OF ENI PRIVATISATION TODAY

The Italian government will unveil on Monday plans for the second stage of the privatisation of Eni, the state oil, gas and energy group. The Treasury is expected to reveal the size of the stake to be sold off, thought to be between 15 and 25 percent. Eni is Italy's largest company, and the sell off will be the country's largest privatisation this year.
-- VOLKSWAGEN APPOINTS BELGIAN TO HEAD SEAT

Volkswagen is to appoint Pierre-Alain de Smedt, currently head of its Brazilian operation, to the post of chairman at its Spanish subsidiary Seat. De Smedt, a Belgian, will be the first non-Spanish chairman of troubled Seat. The company is expected to announce a turnround this year after four years of losses, but current chairman Juan Llorens is believed not to have had the confidence of VW chairman Ferdinand Piech.
